+++
id = "d32870e7"
title = "The Hodge dual trades a blade for its complement"
created = 2026-11-17T18:19:22Z
updated = 2026-11-19T10:22:59Z
tags = ["ga/foundation"]
aliases = ["dual", "Hodge star"]
+++

When the metric is non-degenerate the [[afad7126|The pseudoscalar is the whole space as one blade]] $I = e_1 dots e_n$ is
invertible, and the right Hodge dual of a multivector $A$ is

```typst
A^* = A I^(-1).
```

If $A$ has grade $k$, its dual has grade $n - k$, where $n$ is the dimension.
Geometrically it is the orthogonal complement: a plane becomes its normal
line, and a line through the origin becomes the plane perpendicular to it. The sign convention
matters because the star is only an involution up to sign. In `Cl(4,1)` we have
$I^2 = -1$, hence $I^(-1) = -I$ and

```typst
(A^*)^* = -A, quad "undual"(A) = A I, quad "undual"(A^*) = A.
```

```ocaml
open Geom

let p = Cga.point3 1. 2. 3. in
let star = Cga.dual p in
Blade.grade (Blade.of_int 15)                 (* 4: a four-blade has grade 4 *)
Nx.to_array (Cga.coeff (Cga.undual star) (Blade.of_int 1))  (* 1. *)
```

`undual` must be an explicit function, not `dual` twice, precisely because of
that minus sign. And `dual` raises for a degenerate signature, where $I$ has no
inverse: use [[b5dd2ed2|In a degenerate algebra the dual becomes the complement]] there, and never mix the two.

<figcaption style="text-align:center;font-size:0.85em;opacity:0.7;margin-top:0.4em">The Hodge dual in Cl(3,0,0): the plane B = e12 (grade 2) and its orthogonal complement B* = e3 (grade 1).</figcaption>
</figure>

The dual is how the conformal object layer stores the *lower* of two
representatives. [[decc193a|The working representation stores the lower grade]] is the table;
[[5d4f04c6|Wedge the points, then dualise]] is the recipe that produces those duals from wedges of
points.
